title: Most 'Avocado Oil' Products Aren't Really Avocado Oil
hook: UC Davis testers bought avocado-oil chips, dressings, and mayo off the shelf — most failed purity testing, cut with cheaper seed oils that cost a fraction of the real thing.
key_points: UC Davis researchers tested 54 processed foods labeled as made with avocado oil; 48 failed purity testing.
93% of avocado-oil chips and 100% of salad dressings tested were adulterated with cheaper oils.
Pure avocado oil runs $4–5 a pound versus $0.50–1.50 for seed oils — a strong incentive to cut it.
Brands often buy oil through third-party brokers, so mislabeling can happen upstream of the company on the package.
content_html: Avocado oil has a health halo, and shoppers pay a premium for it — but a new UC Davis test of 54 chips, dressings, and mayonnaises labeled "avocado oil" found that 48 failed purity testing, cut with cheaper substitutes.
extra_html: Published in Applied Food Research, the study found the adulteration was worst in chips (93% failed) and salad dressings (100% failed), with mayonnaise not far behind. The economics explain why: pure avocado oil runs $4–5 a pound, while seed oils cost as little as $0.50–1.50 — a gap wide enough to make quiet substitution tempting. Researchers note that because many brands source oil through third-party brokers rather than pressing it themselves, a company selling "avocado oil" products may not even know its supply has been cut upstream. For now, there's no foolproof label check — buying from brands that publish third-party purity testing is the best available signal.

flashcards.prompt: Why is avocado oil such a common target for food fraud?
flashcards.back_html: Pure avocado oil costs $4–5 a pound, while substitute seed oils cost only $0.50–1.50 — a big price gap that rewards quietly cutting it with cheaper oil.

flashcards.prompt: In the UC Davis testing, how did avocado-oil salad dressings fare?

choices.text: None failed — dressings were the cleanest category

flashcards.explanation_html: Every avocado-oil salad dressing tested was adulterated — the worst-performing category alongside chips, where 93% failed.

flashcards.prompt: Why might a brand sell adulterated avocado oil without intending to deceive?
flashcards.back_html: Many food companies buy their oil through third-party brokers, so a supplier can blend in cheaper oil upstream — the brand on the label may not know.
